title: Neuromorphic Decoding and Dynamical Image Reconstruction from Populations of Spiking Retinal Ganglion Cells
abstract: arXiv:2610.17154v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Decoding visual stimuli from the spiking activity of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) informs both our understanding of the retinal code and the design of visual prostheses. Natural vision is dynamic, yet state-of-the-art decoders mostly reconstruct single frames with artificial neural networks that process dense, continuous-valued signals rather than the retina's sparse, asynchronous spikes. We asked whether dynamic scenes can be reconstructed and tracked entirely within the spike domain, and at what computational cost. We built an end-to-end spiking neural network (SNN) whose neurons integrate the recorded RGC spikes over time. Populations of up to 1836 RGCs were recorded ex vivo from mouse retina on high-density microelectrode arrays while flashed images, moving bars, drifting gratings and randomly moving handwritten digits were presented. translated_title: 从视网膜神经节细胞脉冲群体活动中实现神经形态解码与动态图像重建
translated_abstract: 从视网膜神经节细胞的脉冲活动中解码视觉刺激，既有助于我们理解视网膜编码，也有助于视觉假体的设计。自然视觉是动态的，然而最先进的解码器大多使用人工神经网络重建单帧图像，这些网络处理的是密集的连续值信号，而非视网膜稀疏的异步脉冲。我们探究了动态场景能否完全在脉冲域内被重建和追踪，以及其计算成本如何。我们构建了一个端到端的脉冲神经网络（SNN），其神经元随时间整合记录到的视网膜神经节细胞脉冲。在高密度微电极阵列上对离体小鼠视网膜中多达1836个视网膜神经节细胞的群体进行了记录，同时呈现闪光图像、移动条形、漂移光栅和随机移动的手写数字。对于移动数字，一个共享的脉冲编码器连接两个读出层，其中一个用于重建图像……
tldr: 该研究构建了端到端的脉冲神经网络，首次实现了完全在脉冲域内对视网膜神经节细胞群体活动的解码与动态场景的实时追踪重建，且计算开销极低。
